what: Founder correction -> bounded hypothesis -> held-out later mission -> evidence -> retain/regress, on two supervised GREG bodies driven only through the CLI (signed MISSION, CRITIQUE --correct, ACCEPT/CRITIQUE), including SIGKILL and restart
reality_status: LOCAL-REAL on Linux with test founder keys; consequence-inert (mission workspace files only). Not MAC-VERIFIED, not founder-used.
scenario: Every strategy uses fs.write, so per-capability empirical reliability cannot separate them: mission 1's placeholder note PASSED its check and was appraised, which raises fs.write reliability. Only the founder's judgment identifies it as worthless.

regression_closed.check: Alfonso signs an accepting critique of the alternative's action or closure on 1 eligible later choice(s) with no contrary trial
regression_closed.reason: 1 held-out trial(s) met the declared close condition (founder_accepts) with no contrary trial

founder_review.message: Founder correction says to avoid {'capability': 'fs.write', 'params.content': 'status: TODO'}, but subsequent evidence indicates it may be harmful or overbroad. Founder review recommended.

sequence: m:status-1 on both bodies: baseline chose quick-note ('status: TODO'); check passed; mission achieved
signed CRITIQUE --verdict reject --evidence-type founder_judgment --correct avoid --scope capability --scope params.content --regression ...
m:status-2 (held-out: new mission id, own workspace file): baseline_choice quick-note, correction-aware choice full-note; still CANDIDATE (no verdict yet)
R: greg accept on the full-note action -> trial helped -> RETAINED -> critique.regression_closed (disposition RETAINED)
G: signed CRITIQUE reject on the full-note action -> trial did_not_help -> REGRESSED -> surfaced for founder review; regression stays open
m:status-3: R still chooses full-note (retained correction survives restart); G chooses quick-note (regressed correction no longer influences routing)
both bodies stopped with greg stop --local
negative_evidence: First implementation re-evaluated already-judged applications every tick with a new timestamp; the ledger's fact-identity guard refused it (EventError). Fixed by skipping judged (correction, application) pairs.

First implementation counted the pre-action observation (same tick, same timestamp) as the outcome, so the objective 'checks' close condition never retained. Fixed by ordering evidence by ledger position, not wall-clock time.

Mutation: routing that ignores corrections fails 7/11 correction tests; an evaluator that marks every applied change 'helped' fails the insufficient-evidence, regression and founder-rule contradiction tests (3/11).
